memory_update.text: Add AEP as a direct grid-financing and transmission-rebuild candidate for the tax_credit_infrastructure_implementation node because DOE/LPO financing has already closed for a named 5,000-mile transmission portfolio.

Add FSLR as a domestic-manufacturing and transferable-tax-credit monetization candidate; Section 45X credit realization is a major direct policy linkage that should be tracked separately from generic solar demand.
Add HASI as a project-finance/tax-transferability candidate; its relevance is less about owning equipment and more about structuring financeable clean-energy infrastructure transactions.
Add NXT as a domestic-content implementation supplier; its U.S.-manufactured tracker offering can matter for project-level bonus ITC eligibility and domestic supply-chain compliance.
Add HUBB as a grid component and utility-infrastructure supplier; track whether grid modernization and transmission/substation bottlenecks translate into order growth and margin resilience.

Quanta Services remains highly relevant for EPC/interconnection and grid construction, but because it was already in the seed universe, this pass prioritized incremental additions. Keep PWR in the broader node map.

GE Vernova and transformer-heavy suppliers should be revisited in a separate grid-equipment bottleneck pass; this 5-name limit favored AEP/FSLR/HASI/NXT/HUBB for direct policy implementation diversity.
PWR is a high-priority implementation candidate for grid construction, interconnection, transmission, and utility-scale renewable infrastructure execution.
GEV and ETN should be tracked as scarce electrical-equipment suppliers where transformer, switchgear, and high-voltage equipment lead times may be the real project bottleneck.
HUBB adds less-obvious component exposure to utility T&D, substation, grid protection, and distribution modernization rather than headline clean-energy ownership.
NXT maps to domestic-content compliance for utility-scale solar balance-of-system equipment; relevance depends heavily on final and future Treasury/IRS domestic-content and foreign-entity guidance.

This pass did not include private tax-credit transfer marketplaces, tax-equity banks, legal/compliance advisors, or DOE loan recipients unless they map to a public equipment or infrastructure chokepoint.
HASI should be tracked as a project-finance and tax-credit-monetization implementation candidate, not merely as a renewable yield/finance story.

NXT/Nextpower should be tracked for domestic-content implementation exposure in utility-scale solar, with verification needed against current IRS/Treasury domestic-content rules and customer qualification evidence.
AEP provides a concrete example of DOE infrastructure financing converting policy support into transmission capacity upgrades; monitor similar regulated-utility DOE loan recipients.

HUBB is a second-order grid-capex supplier candidate: stronger mapping if backlog and utility-transmission/substation orders are explicitly tied to grid modernization and federally supported infrastructure projects.

Need a separate pass for public tax-credit buyers, transfer marketplaces, compliance-software vendors, and insurers/banks involved in tax-credit transfer risk; many marketplaces are private, so public-market mapping may be indirect.

node: Tax-credit and infrastructure-spending implementation: clean electricity, domestic manufacturing, grid, nuclear, storage, transmission, and project finance
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: This Layer 1B pass expands the public-company universe around policy-to-project implementation rather than generic clean-energy exposure. The strongest direct mappings found are: regulated transmission asset owners that can turn DOE/LPO financing into rate-base grid upgrades; domestic manufacturers whose products or tax credits directly improve project economics; project-finance specialists that structure clean-energy investments and tax-equity/credit monetization; and grid/component suppliers tied to utility modernization and interconnection bottlenecks. No trading recommendation is implied. Expanded the node universe toward public companies that sit near implementation chokepoints: grid construction labor, high-voltage equipment, electrical distribution equipment, utility T&D components, and domestic-content solar balance-of-system supply. The strongest candidates are not generic clean-energy owners; they are firms whose products or services can determine whether tax-credit-eligible projects reach interconnection, domestic-content compliance, and final construction. Expanded universe toward companies that help policy dollars become buildable, financeable, or compliant assets. The highest-relevance second-order areas in this pass are: project-finance capital providers, domestic-content-enabling solar hardware, regulated transmission rebuild beneficiaries, utility/grid component suppliers, and grid-edge operating software. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
